entries.sanskrit: सप्तमे संशय-च्छेदि प्रतिनन्द्य मुनेर् वचः । पुनः क्षत्त्रा कृता नाना प्रश्नाः सम्यग् उदीरिताः ॥ अथ ते भगवल्-लीला योग-मायोपबृंहिताः\[भा।पु। ३.५.२२\] इत्य्-आदिना माया-गुणैर् लीलया भगवान् सृष्ट्य्-आदि करोतीत्य् एवं ब्रुवाणं मैत्रेयं भारत्या प्रार्थना-रूपया प्रीणयन्न् इवेत्य् अभिप्रायाज्ञानेनाक्षेपात् ॥१॥
word_for_word: saptame saṃśaya-cchedi pratinandya muner vacaḥ
In the seventh chapter
punaḥ kṣattrā kṛtā nānā praśnāḥ samyag udīritāḥ
after honoring the sage’s words that cut doubt
atha te bhagaval-līlā yoga-māyopabṛṃhitāḥ\ ity-ādinā māyā-guṇair līlayā bhagavān sṛṣṭy-ādi karotīty evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ maitreyaṃ bhāratyā prārthanā-rūpayā prīṇayann ivety abhiprāyājñānenākṣepāt
Vidura again properly voiced many questions. When Maitreya had said that the Lord performs creation and the rest through māyā’s qualities as play
entries.literal_english: In the seventh chapter, after honoring the sage’s words that cut doubt, Vidura again properly voiced many questions. When Maitreya had said that the Lord performs creation and the rest through māyā’s qualities as play, Vidura, as though pleasing him with a prayer, challenged the implication that this meaning is already understood.

entries.sanskrit: निर्विकारस्य क्रिया, निर्गुणस्य च गुणाः कथम् ? लीलयेत्य् उक्तिः प्रयोजनाभावं परिहरति, न वस्तु-विरोधम् इति भावः ॥२॥
word_for_word: nirvikārasya kriyā
How can action belong to the changeless
nirguṇasya ca guṇāḥ katham ? līlayety uktiḥ prayojanābhāvaṃ pariharati
and qualities belong to the qualityless? The expression “as play” removes the need for an external purpose
na vastu-virodham iti bhāvaḥ
it does not deny the Lord’s real nature or create a contradiction in the object.
entries.literal_english: How can action belong to the changeless, and qualities belong to the qualityless? The expression “as play” removes the need for an external purpose; it does not deny the Lord’s real nature or create a contradiction in the object.

entries.sanskrit: अर्भकवल् लीलापि न युज्यते वैषम्याद् इत्य् आह---उद्यमयति प्रवर्तयतीत्य् उद्यमः। अर्भकस्य क्रीडायां प्रवृत्ति-हेतुः कामोऽस्ति । अन्यतस् तु वस्त्व्-अन्तरेण बालान्तर-प्रवर्तनेन वा तस्य क्रीडेच्छा भवति । ईश्वरस्य तु स्वतस् तृप्तस्य कथं कामः ? अन्यतः सदा निवृत्तस्य चासङ्गाद् अद्वितीयस्य कथम् अन्यतश् चिक्रीडिषा ? इत्य् अर्थः ॥३॥
word_for_word: arbhakaval līlāpi na yujyate vaiṣamyād ity āha
Even play like a child’s appears unsuitable because it would imply partiality. “Effort” means causing activity. A child plays from desire
udyamayati pravartayatīty udyamaḥ

desire may also arise from another object or from another child’s activity. But the Lord is satisfied in Himself—how could He have desire? Since He is always withdrawn from anything other than Himself
arbhakasya krīḍāyāṃ pravṛtti-hetuḥ kāmo’sti
unattached and nondual
anyatas tu vastv-antareṇa bālāntara-pravartanena vā tasya krīḍecchā bhavati
how could He wish to play with another?
īśvarasya tu svatas tṛptasya kathaṃ kāmaḥ ? anyataḥ sadā nivṛttasya cāsaṅgād advitīyasya katham anyataś cikrīḍiṣā ? ity arthaḥ
how could He wish to play with another?
entries.literal_english: Even play like a child’s appears unsuitable because it would imply partiality. “Effort” means causing activity. A child plays from desire; desire may also arise from another object or from another child’s activity. But the Lord is satisfied in Himself—how could He have desire? Since He is always withdrawn from anything other than Himself, unattached and nondual, how could He wish to play with another?

entries.sanskrit: यच् चोक्तं स्मरन् विश्व-सृजाम् ईशो विज्ञापितम् अधोक्षजे\[भा।पु। ३.६.१\] इत्य्-आदिनाविद्योपाधेर् जीवस्य भोगार्थम् ईश्वरः सृष्ट्य्-आदि करोतीति । तद् अप्य् आक्षेप्तुम् अनुवदति--- अस्राक्षीद् इति । गुण-मयी आत्मनो जीवस्य कर्तृत्व-भोक्तृत्वादि-मोहोत्पादिका या माया, तया सृष्टवान् । तद् उक्तं प्रथमे--- > यया संमोहितो जीव आत्मानं त्रि-गुणात्मकम् । > > परोऽपि मनुतेऽनर्थं तत्-कृतं चाभिपद्यते ॥ \[भा।पु। १.७.५\] > इत्य्-आदिना । अत्र च, अतो भगवतो माया मायिनाम् अपि मोहिनी\[भा।पु। ३.६.३९\] इति । संस्थापयति पालयति । प्रत्यपिधास्यति प्रातिलोम्येन तिरोहितं करिष्यति । पाठान्तरे प्रातिलोम्येनात्मन्य् अभितो धारयिष्यति ॥४॥
word_for_word: yac coktaṃ smaran viśva-sṛjām īśo vijñāpitam adhokṣaje\ ity-ādināvidyopādher jīvasya bhogārtham īśvaraḥ sṛṣṭy-ādi karotīti
Vidura repeats the earlier statement in order to challenge it
tad apy ākṣeptum anuvadati
the Lord creates for the enjoyment of the living being who is deluded by the guṇamayī māyā. That māyā produces the jīva’s delusion of being the doer and enjoyer
asrākṣīd iti

guṇa-mayī ātmano jīvasya kartṛtva-bhoktṛtvādi-mohotpādikā yā māyā
” while “will withdraw” means that He will make the obscuring power disappear in reverse order
tayā sṛṣṭavān

yayā saṃmohito jīva ātmānaṃ tri-guṇātmakam

entries.literal_english: Vidura repeats the earlier statement in order to challenge it: the Lord creates for the enjoyment of the living being who is deluded by the guṇamayī māyā. That māyā produces the jīva’s delusion of being the doer and enjoyer; through it the Lord created. The cited teaching says that the deluded jīva mistakes himself for a three-guṇa being and accepts the resulting harm as his own. Here “establishes” means “protects,” while “will withdraw” means that He will make the obscuring power disappear in reverse order; another reading means that He will hold it completely within Himself.

entries.sanskrit: एतच् च जीवस्याविद्याश्रयत्वे घटेत, न तु तत् संभवतीत्य् आह---देशत इति । योऽसौ देशादिभिर् अविलुप्तावबोध आत्मा जीवः, ब्रह्म-स्वरूपत्वात् । स कथम् अजयाऽविद्यया युज्येत? तत्र देशतो दीप-प्रभाया इव लोपो नास्ति, सर्व-गतत्वात् । न कालतः, विद्युत इव नित्यत्वात् । नावस्थातः, स्मृतिवद् अविक्रियत्वात् । न स्वतः, स्वप्नवत् सत्यत्वात् । नान्यतः, घटादिवद् अद्वितीयत्वात् । एवम् एतैर् यस्य बोधो न लुप्यते, स कथम् अजया युज्येत ? अजा चात्राविद्यैव, न माया, तस्या अवबोधेन विरोधाभावात् ॥५॥
word_for_word: etac ca jīvasyāvidyāśrayatve ghaṭeta
This explanation could apply if the jīva were truly the seat of ignorance
na tu tat saṃbhavatīty āha
but that cannot be so. The self
deśata iti
whose awareness is not diminished by place or anything else
yo’sau deśādibhir aviluptāvabodha ātmā jīvaḥ
is the jīva because it has Brahman’s nature. How could it be joined to beginningless ignorance? There is no loss through place
brahma-svarūpatvāt
because awareness is all-pervading like a lamp’s radiance
sa katham ajayā’vidyayā yujyeta? tatra deśato dīpa-prabhāyā iva lopo nāsti
no loss through time
sarva-gatatvāt
because it is eternal like lightning
na kālataḥ
no loss through condition
vidyuta iva nityatvāt
because it is unchanging like memory
nāvasthātaḥ
no loss through itself
smṛtivad avikriyatvāt
because it is real like a dream
na svataḥ
and no loss through another
svapnavat satyatvāt
because it is nondual like a pot. Since the awareness of such a self is never lost
nānyataḥ
how could it be joined to beginningless ignorance? Here “the beginningless one” means ignorance
ghaṭādivad advitīyatvāt
not the Lord’s māyā
evam etair yasya bodho na lupyate
because awareness does not conflict with māyā itself.
sa katham ajayā yujyeta ? ajā cātrāvidyaiva
because awareness does not conflict with māyā itself.
na māyā
because awareness does not conflict with māyā itself.
tasyā avabodhena virodhābhāvāt
because awareness does not conflict with māyā itself.
entries.literal_english: This explanation could apply if the jīva were truly the seat of ignorance, but that cannot be so. The self, whose awareness is not diminished by place or anything else, is the jīva because it has Brahman’s nature. How could it be joined to beginningless ignorance? There is no loss through place, because awareness is all-pervading like a lamp’s radiance; no loss through time, because it is eternal like lightning; no loss through condition, because it is unchanging like memory; no loss through itself, because it is real like a dream; and no loss through another, because it is nondual like a pot. Since the awareness of such a self is never lost, how could it be joined to beginningless ignorance? Here “the beginningless one” means ignorance, not the Lord’s māyā, because awareness does not conflict with māyā itself.

entries.sanskrit: किं च, ब्रह्म-रूपत्वाद् एव जीवस्य संसारोऽपि न विद्यत इत्य् आक्षिपति । सर्व-क्षेत्रेष्व् अवस्थितो भोक्तापि वस्तुतो भगवान् एव, चिद्-रूपत्वेन तद्-व्यतिरेकाभावात् । एवं च सत्य् अमुष्य जीवस्य दुर्भगत्वम् आनन्दादि-भ्रंशः कर्मभिर् हेतु-भूतैः क्लेशो वा कुतः? कर्म-संबन्धाभावात् । अन्यथेश्वरस्यापि तत्-प्रसङ्गः स्याद् इति भावः ॥६॥
word_for_word: kiṃ ca
Moreover
brahma-rūpatvād eva jīvasya saṃsāro’pi na vidyata ity ākṣipati
because the jīva has Brahman’s nature
sarva-kṣetreṣv avasthito bhoktāpi vastuto bhagavān eva
saṃsāra does not truly exist for it. Although the enjoyer present in every field
cid-rūpatvena tad-vyatirekābhāvāt
the Lord alone exists in reality
evaṃ ca saty amuṣya jīvasya durbhagatvam ānandādi-bhraṃśaḥ karmabhir hetu-bhūtaiḥ kleśo vā kutaḥ? karma-saṃbandhābhāvāt
because consciousness has no difference from Him. Then how could this jīva become unfortunate
anyatheśvarasyāpi tat-prasaṅgaḥ syād iti bhāvaḥ
lose bliss and the like
entries.literal_english: Moreover, because the jīva has Brahman’s nature, saṃsāra does not truly exist for it. Although the enjoyer present in every field, the Lord alone exists in reality, because consciousness has no difference from Him. Then how could this jīva become unfortunate, lose bliss and the like, or suffer through karma? There is no connection with karma; otherwise the same consequence would fall upon the Lord.

word_for_word: ajñānam eva saṅkaṭaṃ durgaṃ tasmin

॥ \[भा।पु। > ६.९.३६\] इति गद्येन तत्र तत्रावितर्क्य-शक्तित्वम् एव सिद्धान्ते योजितम् । तत्र तत्रावितर्क्य-शक्तित्वेन सिद्धान्ते योजितम् । तत्र स्वरूप-शक्तेर् अवितर्क्यत्वं भगवति \[भा।पु। ६.९.३६\] इत्य्-आदिभिर् विशेषणैर् मायायाश् च *आत्म-मायाम्* इत्यनेन दर्शितम् । तत्र स्वरूप-द्वयाभावात् \[भा।पु। ६.९.३५\] इत्य् अस्य तथाप्य् अचिन्त्य-शक्त्या तत्-कर्तृत्वं तद्-अन्तः-पातित्वं च विद्यते इत्य् अर्थः । सम-विषम-मतीनाम् \[भा।पु। ६.९.३७\][^२३] इति तु गद्यं तथाप्य् उच्चावच-बुद्धीनां तथा स्फुरसीति प्रतिपत्त्य्-अर्थं ज्ञेयम् । [^२३]: सम-विषम-मतीनां मतम् अनुसरसि, यथा रज्जु-खण्डः सर्पादि-धियाम्। दुरवबोध इव \[भा।पु। ६.९.३४\] इति प्राक्तन-गद्ये त्व् *अशरीर* इति शरीर-चेष्टां विना,*अशरण* इति भूम्य्-आद्य्-आश्रयं विना इत्य् अर्थः । *अथ तत्र* इत्य्-आदौ स्वकृतेऽपि तस्यापि हेतु-कर्तृत्वाद् योजनीयम् । तस्माद् अत्रापि स्वरूप-शक्तेर् एव प्राधान्यं दर्शितम् । अथ तत्र इत्य् आदौ स्व-कृतेति तस्यापि हेतु-कर्तृत्वं योजनीयं, तस्माद् अत्रापि स्वरूप-शक्तेर् एव प्राबल्यं[^२४] दर्शितम्, अत एव ऋतेऽर्थं यत् प्रतीयेत\[भा।पु। २.९.३३\] इत्य् आदौ मायाया आभास-स्थानीयत्वं प्रदर्श्य, तद्-अस्पृश्यत्वम् एव भगवतो दर्शितम् । त्वम् आद्यः पुरुषः साक्षाद् \[भा।पु। १.७.२३\] इत्य् आदौ, माया व्युदस्य चिच्-छक्त्या इत्य् अनेन च तथा ज्ञापितम् । माया परैत्याभिमुखे च विलज्जामाना\[भा।पु। २.७.४७\] इत्य् अनेन च । [^२४]: प्राधान्यम् इति क्वचित् पाठः। तद् एवं भगवति तद्-विरोधं परिहृत्य जीवेऽप्य् अविद्या-सम्बन्धम् अतर्क्यत्वेन दर्शिततया तन् माययैव समादधाति । ईश्वरस्य इति यद् इत्य् अनेनैव सम्बध्यते । अर्थ-वशाद् अत्र च तृतीयया परिणम्यते । यत् यथा ईश्वरस्य स्वरूप-ज्ञानादिभिः समर्थस्य, अत एव विमुक्तस्य \[जीवस्य[^२५]\] कार्पण्यं तत्-तत्-प्रकाश-तिरोभावः, तथा बन्धनं दर्शित-गुण-मय-जाल-प्रवेशश् च भवतीति । तद् उक्तं---तत्-सङ्ग-भ्रंशितैश्वर्यं \[भा।पु। ६.५.१५\] इति । [^२५]: परमात्म-सन्दर्भस्य पाठः। तद् एवं सर्वम् अभिप्रेत्य श्रुतयोऽप्य् आहुः---स यद् अजया त्व् अजां \[भा।पु। १०.८७.३८\] इत्य्-आदाव् अपेत-भग इति च । अत्र मूल-पद्ये भगवतो मायेत्य् अनेन भगवत्त्वं मायिकम्[^२६] इत्य् आयातम् । इन्द्रस्य मायेत्य् अत्र यथेन्द्रत्वम् एवं पूर्वत्रापि ज्ञेयम् ॥९॥ \[परमात्म-सन्दर्भ २५, ९०\] [^२६]: \"भगवत्त्वं त्व् अमायिकं\" इति, \"भगवत्-तत्त्वम् अमायिकं\" इति च द्वौ पाठौ परमात्म-सन्दर्भे ड्र्श्येते।

Since mere consciousness alone cannot explain the jīva either
seyam iti
Maitreya accepts the jīva’s divine status and says “this.” The power by which cosmic creation and the rest occur is the Lord’s inconceivable self-power called māyā. Because it is beyond reasoning
yayā viśva-sṛṣṭy-ādikaṃ bhavati
it is itself inconceivable. Although both the Lord and His māyā are inconceivable
seyaṃbhagavato’cintya-svarūpa-śakter māyākhyā śaktiḥ
the phrase “the Lord’s māyā” shows that māyā is His external power
yat yā nayena tarkeṇa virudhyate tarkātītatayā seyam apy acintyety arthaḥ
whereas the Lord’s own power is internal
yadyapy evaṃ dvayor apy acintyatvaṃ

therefore the external guṇas and their effects—maintenance and the rest—do not touch Him. The cited Tantric explanation means that whatever is not opposed to the Lord through māyā is not made an object of contradiction
tathāpi bhagavato māyety anena vyaktatvāt svarūpa-śakter antaraṅgatvād bahiraṅgāyā māyāyā guṇaiḥ sattvādibhis tat-kāryaiḥ sthāpanādibhiś ca nāsau spṛśyata ity arthaḥ
and what is not opposed to Him is not thereby made wholly nonexistent. The examples from the Purāṇa establish that the Lord creates
tantreṇa cāyam arthaḥ
maintains and destroys with qualities while remaining without limiting qualities
yat yathā māyayā yena bhagavatā saha na viruddhyate
because His inconceivable power accomplishes both sides. The same reasoning removes the charge of partiality
nāsau virodha-viṣayī-kriyata iti
the Lord’s self-power is primary
yat yā yena bhagavatā na virudhyate
while māyā appears as an external reflection. The note then explains that the jīva’s bondage

poverty and obscuration of knowledge are also arranged through that same inconceivable māyā. Thus the Lord’s divine status is not produced by māyā
evam eva ṣaṣṭhe navamādhyāye
rather

entries.literal_english: Since mere consciousness alone cannot explain the jīva either, Maitreya accepts the jīva’s divine status and says “this.” The power by which cosmic creation and the rest occur is the Lord’s inconceivable self-power called māyā. Because it is beyond reasoning, it is itself inconceivable. Although both the Lord and His māyā are inconceivable, the phrase “the Lord’s māyā” shows that māyā is His external power, whereas the Lord’s own power is internal; therefore the external guṇas and their effects—maintenance and the rest—do not touch Him. The cited Tantric explanation means that whatever is not opposed to the Lord through māyā is not made an object of contradiction; and what is not opposed to Him is not thereby made wholly nonexistent. The examples from the Purāṇa establish that the Lord creates, maintains and destroys with qualities while remaining without limiting qualities, because His inconceivable power accomplishes both sides. The same reasoning removes the charge of partiality: the Lord’s self-power is primary, while māyā appears as an external reflection. The note then explains that the jīva’s bondage, poverty and obscuration of knowledge are also arranged through that same inconceivable māyā. Thus the Lord’s divine status is not produced by māyā; rather, His māyā belongs to one who is already Bhagavān, while the jīva’s limitation is the concealment of powers that are otherwise present.

entries.sanskrit: उत्तरम् अभिनन्दन्न् आत्मनः कृतार्थताम् आविष्करोति---सञ्छिन्न इति षड्भिः । चिद्-रूपत्वाविशेषेऽपि कथम् ईश्वरस्य जगत्-कर्तृत्वादि, कथं वा जीवस्य संसारः ? इति यः संशयो ममासीत्, स तव सूक्तं सोपपत्तिकं वाक्यम् एवासिः खड्गस् तेन सञ्छिन्नः । अत इदानीं मे मन उभयत्रापीश्वर-स्वातन्त्र्ये जीव-पारतन्त्र्ये च सम्प्रधावति सम्यक् प्रविशति । एवं वाविलुप्तावबोध-रूपस्यात्मनः कथम् अविद्यया बन्धः, कुतो वा तन्-निवृत्तिः ? इति संशयः । उभयत्रेति, बन्धे मोक्षे चेत्य् अर्थः ॥१५॥
word_for_word: uttaram abhinandann ātmanaḥ kṛtārthatām āviṣkaroti
Vidura welcomes the answer and reveals that he has become fulfilled. The doubt was
sañchinna iti ṣaḍbhiḥ
if Lord and jīva are equally consciousness
cid-rūpatvāviśeṣe’pi katham īśvarasya jagat-kartṛtvādi

how can the Lord create the world while the jīva undergoes saṃsāra? Your well-reasoned words were the sword that cut it. Now my mind clearly enters both truths—the Lord’s independence and the jīva’s dependence. The remaining doubt was how the self
kathaṃ vā jīvasya saṃsāraḥ ? iti yaḥ saṃśayo mamāsīt
whose awareness is not lost
sa tava sūktaṃ sopapattikaṃ vākyam evāsiḥ khaḍgas tena sañchinnaḥ
can be bound by ignorance and how that bondage can end
ata idānīṃ me mana ubhayatrāpīśvara-svātantrye jīva-pāratantrye ca sampradhāvati samyak praviśati
“both” means bondage and liberation.
evaṃ vāviluptāvabodha-rūpasyātmanaḥ katham avidyayā bandhaḥ
“both” means bondage and liberation.
kuto vā tan-nivṛttiḥ ? iti saṃśayaḥ
“both” means bondage and liberation.
ubhayatreti
“both” means bondage and liberation.
bandhe mokṣe cety arthaḥ

entries.literal_english: Vidura welcomes the answer and reveals that he has become fulfilled. The doubt was: if Lord and jīva are equally consciousness, how can the Lord create the world while the jīva undergoes saṃsāra? Your well-reasoned words were the sword that cut it. Now my mind clearly enters both truths—the Lord’s independence and the jīva’s dependence. The remaining doubt was how the self, whose awareness is not lost, can be bound by ignorance and how that bondage can end; “both” means bondage and liberation.

entries.sanskrit: यस्मात् त्वया साधु व्याहृतम् । किं तत् ? हरेः शक्तिर् या आत्म-माया जीव-विषया माया तद्-अयनं तद्-आश्रयम् एतद् दुर्भगत्वादिकं भातीति । यत् यस्मात् स्व-शिरश् छेदादि-वद् अपार्थम् अवस्तु-भूतं निर्मूलं मूल-शून्यं च । यस्माद् अस्य मूलं विश्वस्य मूलं स्वाज्ञानं बहिर् विना नास्ति ॥१६॥
word_for_word: yasmāt tvayā sādhu vyāhṛtam
You have spoken well. The Lord’s power called the self-māyā
kiṃ tat ? hareḥ śaktir yā ātma-māyā jīva-viṣayā māyā tad-ayanaṃ tad-āśrayam etad durbhagatvādikaṃ bhātīti
directed toward the jīva and resting upon it
yat yasmāt sva-śiraś chedādi-vad apārtham avastu-bhūtaṃ nirmūlaṃ mūla-śūnyaṃ ca
makes this apparent misfortune shine forth. What appears is like the false cutting of one’s own head
yasmād asya mūlaṃ viśvasya mūlaṃ svājñānaṃ bahir vinā nāsti
it is purposeless
unreal and without a root. The root of this appearance is the world’s own ignorance
entries.literal_english: You have spoken well. The Lord’s power called the self-māyā, directed toward the jīva and resting upon it, makes this apparent misfortune shine forth. What appears is like the false cutting of one’s own head: it is purposeless, unreal and without a root. The root of this appearance is the world’s own ignorance, and apart from the external power there is no other root.

entries.sanskrit: अल्प-ज्ञत्वात् पूर्वं मम संशयो जात इत्य् आह---यश् चेति । मूढतमो देहाद्य्-आसक्तो यश् च बुद्धेः प्रकृतेः परम् ईश्वरं प्राप्तः, तौ सुखं यथ भवति तथा एधेते जीवत इत्य् अर्थः, संशय-क्लेशाभावात् । यस् तु दुःखानुसन्धानेन प्रपञ्चं जिहासति स्वानन्द-संवेदनाभावाद् धातुं न शक्नोति, स तु क्लिश्यतीत्य् अर्थः ॥१७॥
word_for_word: alpa-jñatvāt pūrvaṃ mama saṃśayo jāta ity āha
He says that my doubt arose from limited knowledge. The person sunk in the deepest delusion and attached to the body
yaś ceti
and the person who has reached the Lord beyond material intelligence
mūḍhatamo dehādy-āsakto yaś ca buddheḥ prakṛteḥ param īśvaraṃ prāptaḥ
live and flourish according to their respective condition
tau sukhaṃ yatha bhavati tathā edhete jīvata ity arthaḥ
because they are free from the torment of doubt. But one who wants to abandon the world by dwelling on suffering cannot remain steady
saṃśaya-kleśābhāvāt
because he lacks direct experience of his own bliss
yas tu duḥkhānusandhānena prapañcaṃ jihāsati svānanda-saṃvedanābhāvād dhātuṃ na śaknoti
therefore he suffers.
sa tu kliśyatīty arthaḥ
therefore he suffers.
therefore he suffers.
entries.literal_english: He says that my doubt arose from limited knowledge. The person sunk in the deepest delusion and attached to the body, and the person who has reached the Lord beyond material intelligence, live and flourish according to their respective condition, because they are free from the torment of doubt. But one who wants to abandon the world by dwelling on suffering cannot remain steady, because he lacks direct experience of his own bliss; therefore he suffers.

entries.sanskrit: प्रपञ्च-प्रतीति-पराणोदन-मात्रं कियत् ? यतः यत्-सेवयेति व्यसनार्दन इत्य् आनुषङ्गिक एवासौ यस्य गुण इत्य् अर्थः ॥१९॥

entries.sanskrit: अहो दुर्लभं प्राप्तं मयेत्य् आह---दुरापा दुर्लभा । वैकुण्ठस्य विष्णोस् तल्-लोकस्य वा वर्त्मसु मार्ग-भूतेषु महत्सु । यत्र येषु । महत्-सेवया हरि-कथा-श्रवणं, ततो हरौ प्रेम, तेन च देहाद्य्-अनुसन्धानम् अपि निवर्तत इति तात्पर्यम् ॥२०॥

entries.sanskrit: प्राणादयः पञ्च नागादयः पञ्चेत्य् एवं दश-विधः । इन्द्रियाणि च । अर्थाश् च इन्द्रियाणि चेति पुनर् उक्तिस् तद्-देवता-लक्षणार्था, तत्-सहितः । सर्वोपबृंहकत्वात् प्राणस्य तत्-साहित्यम् । एवं त्रि-वृत् त्रि-विधः प्राणस् त्वयेरित उक्तः । तस्य विभूतीर् ब्रह्माद्या विसर्ग-शब्द-वाच्याः ॥२३॥
word_for_word: prāṇādayaḥ pañca nāgādayaḥ pañcety evaṃ daśa-vidhaḥ

The five beginning with prāṇa and the five beginning with Nāga make ten kinds. The senses and their objects are also included. The repeated mention of “objects and senses” identifies their presiding deities
indriyāṇi ca
together with them. Because prāṇa supports everything
arthāś ca indriyāṇi ceti punar uktis tad-devatā-lakṣaṇārthā
the senses and their deities are said to accompany it. Thus the prāṇa described by you is threefold through the three divisions
tat-sahitaḥ
its manifestations
sarvopabṛṃhakatvāt prāṇasya tat-sāhityam
beginning with Brahmā
evaṃ tri-vṛt tri-vidhaḥ prāṇas tvayerita uktaḥ
are denoted by the word creation.
tasya vibhūtīr brahmādyā visarga-śabda-vācyāḥ
are denoted by the word creation.
are denoted by the word creation.
entries.literal_english: The five beginning with prāṇa and the five beginning with Nāga make ten kinds. The senses and their objects are also included. The repeated mention of “objects and senses” identifies their presiding deities, together with them. Because prāṇa supports everything, the senses and their deities are said to accompany it. Thus the prāṇa described by you is threefold through the three divisions; its manifestations, beginning with Brahmā, are denoted by the word creation.

entries.literal_english: The seventh chapter has again stated the many questions of Vidura, after he honored the sage’s words that cut doubt.
